messages:
Taylor (Customer): hey team — during a product walkthrough just now we started seeing a bunch of 429s against the /v1/generate endpoint and a couple of 401s interspersed. demo was in us-west. request ids: r-9f3c, r-9f3d, r-9f40. we're on the free tier but only doing a ~30‑user demo. any quick fixes?

Jules (Support): sorry to hear that, Taylor. can you confirm which API key you used (masked is fine), and roughly what cadence/size the demo requests were? also, do you have the exact 429 response body copy/paste?

Taylor (Customer): key starts with rk_live_****. pattern was: many short chat completions — ~2–3 turns each — roughly 12 concurrent requests at peak, maybe 600 tokens per minute total. 429 body: {\"error\":{\"message\":\"Rate limit exceeded\",\"type\":\"rate_limit\"}}. 401 example: {\"error\":{\"message\":\"Unauthorized\"}} — appeared twice only.

Jules (Support): thanks. that 429 is classic quota exhaustion on free tier burst limits. the 401s are odd — could be a transient key rotation or clock skew. forwarding to SRE for correlation with quota counters and recent key rotations. @Sam can you pull the token/quotas and any key rotation events for Taylor's key (rk_live_****) around now?

Sam (SRE): on it. pulling logs. quick heads-up: we had an automated key-rotation job earlier today for keys created before 2024-11-01; it only touches service keys but we'll verify. also seeing ephemeral spike from a single IP that hit continuous-burst protection which can surface as 429s then a backend auth layer sometimes throws 401 if a rotated key is still propagating to an edge.

Sam (SRE): found the trace for r-9f3c/r-9f3d — quota counters showed free-tier burst window hit ~2s before the first 429, then automatic fallback to short-term rate-limit policy. 401s correlate with our edge cache invalidation window — the key was rotated earlier for another customer but racey propagation caused a handful of auth failures for incoming requests that hit certain POPs. not a fault on Taylor's key.

Jules (Support): TL;DR: you hit the free-tier burst cap; we also had an unrelated propagation race that caused a couple of 401s. we can do two things now: (1) apply a temporary intraday burst uplift for your demo (one-day rule), (2) suggest a short repro script and some client-side best-practices to avoid hitting the burst cap again. which do you want?

Taylor (Customer): would appreciate uplift for the rest of today — demo still running. repro script would be great too so we can avoid this in future.

Priya (Sales): @Jules — we can approve a one-day upgrade to the "demo burst" allowance (adds ~3x burst capacity) but need a quick sales note and email from Taylor confirming company and demo window. I'll take care of the billing flag. Taylor — can you confirm company name and timezone for the window?

Taylor (Customer): Acme Widgets, PST. window: now until 23:59 PST today. email sent to priya@redwood.ai with demo details.

Jules (Support): copying the steps I'm going to take: (a) request temporary uplift from quota service (1-day, +3x burst), (b) ask infra to check the edge propagation flap and patch mitigation, (c) provide Taylor a minimal repro script and client recommendations.

ops-bot: quota-request accepted, ticket Q-45219 created, pending manual approval by sales.

Priya (Sales): approved Q-45219. tagging billing team for flag.

Jules (Support): uplift applied — you should see reduced 429s within 60s. Taylor, please confirm if errors drop.

Taylor (Customer): 2 minutes in — much better. no 429s currently. thanks! those two 401s were painless — let us know if you want logs.

Jules (Support): excellent. here is a short repro script you can use to emulate steady concurrent load and confirm behavior locally. run from a machine in the same region as your demo to get realistic results: 

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
API_KEY=\"rk_live_****\"
for i in {1..12}; do 
  (curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" 
    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" 
    -d '{\"model\":\"rw-1-small\",\"input\":\"hi\"}' 
  & )
done
wait
```

Jules (Support): client best-practices: (1) reuse connections, (2) limit concurrent parallelism to what the plan supports — for free tier keep conc <= 8, (3) implement exponential backoff with jitter on 429s, (4) pre-warm with a few low-cost requests before peak.

Sam (SRE): infra note: we've flagged edge propagation race. short-term mitigation: increase auth cache TTL and avoid simultaneous manual key rotations across POPs. ops will deploy a small patch in the next maintenance window to reduce window of 401 flakiness. deploy-bot: starting canary of auth-cache-ttl-adjust (rollout id: rl-887).

deploy-bot: canary rollout rl-887 started at commit 3a9c4d; monitoring hooks attached.

Taylor (Customer): thanks — helpful. if we move to paid plan what's the safe concurrency target? we expect demo to scale later.

Priya (Sales): paid tiers start with predictable burst and increased concurrency. recommend Dedicated for steady throughput but for smaller teams the Paid Pro plan bumps the burst and quota 10x vs free. I can send a tailored quote if you want to discuss SLA and reserved capacity.

Jules (Support): final notes: (1) uplift will expire at 23:59 PST — we'll notify you 1h before expiry, (2) you can avoid the 401 risk by not rotating keys during demos; if you need key rotation we can coordinate a low-risk schedule, (3) if you plan frequent demos we can set up a recurring demo-burst add-on or an automated sales review to provision Dedicated for demos.

Taylor (Customer): perfect. appreciate the quick response and the temporary bump. will run the repro script and report back if anything else pops up.

Priya (Sales): noted — I'll follow up with a pricing email and a one-time invoice option for the demo uplift if you want to convert it to a paid short-term plan.

Jules (Support): closing the loop here but leaving Q-45219 open until uplift expiry and deploy monitoring clears. feel free to re-open if you see anything. :thumbsup:
